title: Add due dates to action items
analysis: Action items are more useful when they carry a due date. The skill should ask for one when it is missing from the notes instead of leaving it out.

instructionEdits.content:
1. Summary: Two or three sentences capturing the purpose and outcome of the meeting.
  2. Decisions: A bulleted list of decisions that were made.
  3. Action items: A bulleted list of tasks, each with an owner and a due date. If the notes do not mention a due date, mark it as TBD and ask the user for it.

title: Clarify when to use the skill
analysis: The agent-facing description should tell agents that the skill also handles call transcripts and Slack threads, so it gets picked up in those situations.

agentFacingDescriptionEdit.content: Turns raw meeting notes, call transcripts or Slack threads into a structured summary with decisions and action items (with owners and due dates).

title: Hand over skill maintenance to Leila
analysis: Leila now runs the weekly team meetings and should be able to maintain the skill. Luke no longer attends them and asked to be removed.

title: Schedule follow-ups with the Team Calendar tool
analysis: Meeting notes often end with a follow-up meeting to organize. The skill should offer to create the event with the Team Calendar tool instead of leaving it to the user.

instructionEdits.content: Keep the original wording where possible and do not invent information that is not in the notes. When the notes mention a follow-up meeting, offer to schedule it with using the attendees and date from the notes.

title: Expand acronyms using the Team Glossary
analysis: Summaries reuse acronyms from the notes verbatim, which readers outside the team do not understand. The skill should look them up in the Team Glossary and expand them on first use.

instructionEdits.content: When given raw meeting notes, produce a structured summary. Expand acronyms on first use by looking them up in .

title: Describe the skill for members
analysis: Members browsing skills only see the user-facing description. It should say what to paste in and what comes back, not just what the skill does internally.

suggestion.userFacingDescription: Paste raw meeting notes, a call transcript or a Slack thread and get back a clean summary with the decisions and the action items, each with an owner and a due date.

title: Rename to match its scope
analysis: The skill now covers call transcripts and Slack threads, not only meeting notes, and its output is a decisions-and-actions summary. The name should say so.

title: Delete this skill
analysis: Nobody has sent meeting notes through this skill in three months; the team now formats notes directly in the meeting tool.

title: Stop agents from auto-picking it
analysis: Agents keep discovering this skill on their own and applying it to messages that are not meeting notes. Keeping it available to members, but not to agents, lets people choose it when it fits.

title: Pause self-improvement
analysis: The team is rewriting the meeting template this month. Suggestions based on conversations using the old template would only add noise until the rewrite lands.
